newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary minister sees 97 budget gap 5.3 pct of GDP.
newsitem.headline: Hungary minister sees 97 budget gap 5.3 pct of GDP.

text.p: Hungary's accounting changes are likely to increase the general budget deficit to 5.3 percent of GDP next year from this year's four percent target, but the change is of a technical nature, Finance Minister Peter Medgyessy said on Wednesday.
"This means a 5.3 percent deficit next year, but in comparative structure it only corresponds to three percent," Medgyessy told a conference of municipality officials.
"The accounting changes between the central state budget and the National Bank of Hungary will not demand any special economic policy steps," he added.

The devaluation losses on Hungary's foreign debt have only appeared in the books of the National Bank of Hungary so far, but from 1997 the general state budget will take over these loans which make the burdens of the budget more transparent, but will not increase them, Medgyessy said.
The general state budget includes the central state budget, the social security system and other items.
Medgyessy said Hungary plans to overhaul the social security system as its soaring deficit could make it unfundable next year without urgent reforms.
He added that the social security deficit could be as high as 60 billion forints this year, compared with a target of 17.8 billion forints.
